Run an agent by passing YAML inline.

Returns:
  { success, agent, output, chains, pending_chains, duration_ms }

Note: chains: with relative next_agent paths require /run-file instead (path resolution needs a base directory).

Run an agent from a YAML file path on the server's disk.

Returns:
  { success, agent, output, chains, pending_chains, duration_ms }

- chains: array of auto-chain results (nested, recursive)
- pending_chains: array of manual chains awaiting approval via POST /approve-chain

body.raw:
{
  "yaml": "name: Blog to Video Agent
description: Converts a blog post into a teaching video — fetches content, plans slides, generates images and narration, creates a Canva presentation, and exports an MP4.

instructions: |
  You are a teaching video producer. Follow each step exactly and pass outputs
  from one step into the next. Do not skip steps or combine them.

params:
  - name: blog_url
    description: Full URL of the blog post to convert into a video
    default: https://www.openenthrium.com/blog/ai-telegram-bot-agent.html

llm:
  provider: openai
  model: gpt-4o

connectors:
  - connection_name: Blog
    connection_type: restApi
  - connection_name: OpenAI
    connection_type: restApi
  - connection_name: Canva
    connection_type: restApi

steps:
  - name: Fetch Blog Content
    use: Blog
    content: |
      GET {{blog_url}}
      Extract all heading and paragraph text. Return the full article text only — no HTML tags.

  - name: Plan Slides
    content: |
      You are a teaching video scriptwriter. Convert the blog content into exactly 6 slides.
      Output a JSON array — one object per slide with these exact keys:
      {
        "slide_number": 1,
        "title": "short slide title (max 8 words)",
        "bullets": ["point 1", "point 2", "point 3"],
        "narration": "20-30 words spoken aloud for this slide — conversational and clear",
        "image_prompt": "detailed DALL-E 3 prompt for a professional, relevant background image"
      }
      Slide 1 = title and intro. Slides 2-5 = one key concept each. Slide 6 = summary and next steps.
      Output only the JSON array, nothing else.

  - name: Generate Slide Images
    use: OpenAI
    content: |
      For each of the 6 slides, POST /images/generations with:
        model: dall-e-3
        prompt: the slide's image_prompt
        size: 1792x1024
        quality: standard
        n: 1
      Collect all 6 image URLs in slide order. Return them as a numbered list.

  - name: Generate Narration Audio
    use: OpenAI
    content: |
      Join all 6 slide narrations in order into one script, separated by " ... " between slides.
      POST /audio/speech with:
        model: tts-1
        voice: nova
        input: the combined narration script
      Return the audio file path where it was saved.

  - name: Create Canva Presentation
    use: Canva
    content: |
      POST /designs with body:
        { "design_type": { "type": "preset", "name": "Presentation" } }
      Save the returned design ID. This is the blank presentation to fill with slides.

  - name: Upload Images to Canva
    use: Canva
    content: |
      For each of the 6 slide image URLs from step 3, POST /assets with the image URL.
      Use name "slide-1.png" through "slide-6.png".
      Collect and return all 6 Canva asset IDs in order.

  - name: Upload Audio to Canva
    use: Canva
    content: |
      POST /assets to upload the narration audio file saved in step 4.
      Use name "narration.mp3". Return the Canva audio asset ID.

  - name: Add Slides to Design
    use: Canva
    content: |
      For each of the 6 slides, POST /designs/{designId}/pages:
        - Set the slide image asset as the page background
        - Add a text element for the slide title
        - Add a text element for the bullet points
      Add the narration audio as the design audio track.

  - name: Export Video
    use: Canva
    content: |
      POST /exports with the design ID and body: { "format": { "type": "mp4" } }
      Poll GET /exports/{exportId} every 10 seconds until status is "success".
      Return the final MP4 download URL.

  - name: Report
    content: |
      The teaching video is ready. Provide:
      - The Canva MP4 download URL
      - A summary of each slide title
      - Total number of slides and estimated video length
",
  "params": {},
  "input": null
}

request.description:
Converts a blog post into a teaching video — fetches content, plans slides, generates images and narration, creates a Canva presentation, and exports an MP4.
Connectors: Blog (restApi), OpenAI (restApi), Canva (restApi)

  "yaml": "name: Drive Manager
description: Read, write, and organize files in Google Drive
instructions: |
  You are a file organization agent with access to Google Drive.
  Help find, list, organize, and summarize files and folders.
  Always confirm before making any write or delete operations.
  Complete all steps fully before writing your report.
steps:
  - name: List Files
    content: |
      Call the Google Drive connector:
      GET /files with params:
      {
        "orderBy": "modifiedTime desc",
        "pageSize": "20",
        "fields": "files(id,name,mimeType,size,modifiedTime,parents)"
      }
      Note each file's name, type, size, and last modified date.

  - name: Identify Unorganized Files
    content: |
      From the listed files, identify any files sitting loose in the root that could be moved into folders.
      Group them by type (documents, spreadsheets, images, PDFs, other).

  - name: Report
    content: |
      Produce a Drive summary:
      - Total files and folders found
      - Breakdown by file type
      - List of files that are unorganized in root
      - Recommended folder structure to organize them
connectors:
  - connection_name: My Google Drive
    connection_type: google-drive
",
  "params": {},
  "input": null
}

{
  "yaml": "name: Email Assistant
description: Summarize inbox and send a follow-up email
instructions: |
  You are an email assistant. Read the inbox via IMAP and send emails via SMTP.
  Draft professional, concise messages. Never send without confirming recipient and subject.
  Complete all steps fully before writing your report.
steps:
  - name: Read Inbox
    content: |
      Call the Gmail connector:
      GET /messages with params: { "labelIds": "UNREAD", "maxResults": "10" }
      Then for each message id returned, call:
      GET /messages/<id> with params: { "format": "metadata", "metadataHeaders": "From,Subject,Date" }
      Collect sender, subject, date, and snippet for each email.

  - name: Draft and Send Reply
    content: |
      From the unread emails, identify the one that most urgently needs a reply.
      Draft a professional acknowledgement reply. Then send it by calling:
      POST /messages/send
      with body: { "raw": "<base64url-encoded RFC 2822 message>" }
      Construct the raw field as: base64url("From: me\r\nTo: <sender>\r\nSubject: Re: <subject>\r\n\r\n<body>")

  - name: Report
    content: |
      Summarize what was done:
      - Number of unread emails found
      - Brief summary of each email (sender, subject, urgency level)
      - Which email was replied to and why
      - Confirm the reply was sent successfully
connectors:
  - connection_name: My Email
    connection_type: gmail-rest
",
  "params": {},
  "input": null
}

  You are a document analysis agent. Extract text from images using the Azure Vision connector,

      Produce a document analysis result:

      - Full raw text extracted
      - Any low-confidence regions or unreadable sections
      - Suggested next action (e.g. file, process payment, follow up)
connectors:
  - connection_name: Azure Vision

  "yaml": "name: Database Analyst
description: Query a SQL database and summarize results in plain English
instructions: |
  You are a database analyst with read access to a SQL database.
  Run SELECT queries to explore the schema and answer data questions.
  Always explain results clearly in plain English.
  Do not run INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DROP statements.
  Complete all steps fully before writing your report.
steps:
  - name: Explore Schema
    content: |
      Run the following queries one at a time:
      1. List all tables in the database
      2. For each table, fetch the column names and data types
      3. Count the rows in each table
  - name: Analyze Key Data
    content: |
      From the largest table found:
      - Fetch the 5 most recently created rows (use created_at or id DESC if available)
      - Calculate row counts grouped by any status or category column if one exists
      - Identify any columns with NULL values and count how many rows are affected
  - name: Report
    content: |
      Produce a database summary in plain English:
      - Tables found and their row counts
      - Schema of the largest table (column names and types)
      - Sample of 5 recent records
      - Data quality observations (nulls, unexpected values)
      - Suggested queries for further analysis
connectors:
  - connection_name: My Database
    connection_type: postgresql
",
  "params": {},
  "input": null

      Call the Telegram connector:
      GET /getUpdates with params: { "limit": "10", "allowed_updates": "message" }

      Remember the chat_id from the most recent message — you will use it to send the reply.
      If no updates are found, note that the bot has no recent messages and skip the next step.

  - name: Send Summary Notification
    content: |
      Compose a brief summary of the recent messages.
      Use the chat_id from the most recent update (from Step 2).
      Send it via the Telegram connector:
      POST /sendMessage with body:
      {
        "chat_id": <chat_id from Step 2>,
        "text": "<your summary message>",
        "parse_mode": "Markdown"
      }

  - name: Report
    content: |
      Summarize what was done:
      - Bot name and username confirmed
      - Number of recent messages read
      - Summary of message content
      - Notification sent to chat_id (confirm with message_id returned)

{
  "yaml": "name: Video Creator Agent
description: Generates a short teaching video on any topic — creates a slide plan, generates images and narration via OpenAI, assembles and exports an MP4 via Canva.

instructions: |
  You are a video production agent. Follow each step in order and pass outputs
  from one step into the next. Do not skip steps or combine them.

params:
  - name: topic
    description: The topic or title of the video to create
    default: "How AI Agents Work"

llm:
  provider: openai
  model: gpt-4o

connectors:
  - connection_name: OpenAI
    connection_type: restApi
  - connection_name: Canva
    connection_type: restApi

steps:
  - name: Plan Slides
    content: |
      You are a teaching video scriptwriter. Create exactly 5 slides for a short video on: {{topic}}
      Output a JSON array — one object per slide with these exact keys:
      {
        "slide_number": 1,
        "title": "short slide title (max 8 words)",
        "bullets": ["point 1", "point 2", "point 3"],
        "narration": "20-30 words spoken aloud for this slide — conversational and clear",
        "image_prompt": "detailed DALL-E 3 prompt for a professional, relevant background image"
      }
      Slide 1 = title and intro. Slides 2-4 = one key concept each. Slide 5 = summary and takeaway.
      Output only the JSON array, nothing else.

  - name: Generate Slide Images
    use: OpenAI
    content: |
      For each of the 5 slides, POST /images/generations with:
        model: dall-e-3
        prompt: the slide's image_prompt
        size: 1792x1024
        quality: standard
        n: 1
      Collect all 5 image URLs in slide order. Return them as a numbered list.

  - name: Generate Narration Audio
    use: OpenAI
    content: |
      Join all 5 slide narrations in order into one script, separated by " ... " between slides.
      POST /audio/speech with:
        model: tts-1
        voice: nova
        input: the combined narration script
      Return the audio file path where it was saved.

  - name: Create Canva Presentation
    use: Canva
    content: |
      POST /designs with body:
        { "design_type": { "type": "preset", "name": "Presentation" } }
      Save the returned design ID. This is the blank presentation to fill with slides.

  - name: Upload Images to Canva
    use: Canva
    content: |
      For each of the 5 slide image URLs from step 2, POST /assets with the image URL.
      Use name "slide-1.png" through "slide-5.png".
      Collect and return all 5 Canva asset IDs in order.

  - name: Upload Audio to Canva
    use: Canva
    content: |
      POST /assets to upload the narration audio file saved in step 3.
      Use name "narration.mp3". Return the Canva audio asset ID.

  - name: Add Slides to Design
    use: Canva
    content: |
      For each of the 5 slides, POST /designs/{designId}/pages:
        - Set the slide image asset as the page background
        - Add a text element for the slide title
        - Add a text element for the bullet points
      Add the narration audio as the design audio track.

  - name: Export Video
    use: Canva
    content: |
      POST /exports with the design ID and body: { "format": { "type": "mp4" } }
      Poll GET /exports/{exportId} every 10 seconds until status is "success".
      Return the final MP4 download URL.

  - name: Report
    content: |
      The video is ready. Provide:
      - The Canva MP4 download URL
      - A summary of each slide title
      - Topic covered and estimated video length
",
  "params": {},
  "input": null
}

request.description:
Generates a short teaching video on any topic — creates a slide plan, generates images and narration via OpenAI, assembles and exports an MP4 via Canva.
Connectors: OpenAI (restApi), Canva (restApi)

      ## Key Findings

      ## Trends
      [Top themes identified across sources]

      ## Sources
      [Numbered list: title, publication, URL for each cited source]

      ## Recommendations
